question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions use declared prior learning: q01 directly retrieves vector-triangle equilibrium and q07 mixes density with coplanar equilibrium.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: prior retrieval, definition and unit diagnostics, proportional comparison, direct geometric density, material-volume interpretation, then mixed density and equilibrium

evidence_basis.originality_note: All contexts, wording, values and figure briefs are original. Mapped evidence grounds only the definition, unit-conversion, geometric-volume and multi-step density demands.

questions.prompt: Three coplanar forces keep an object in equilibrium. Describe how to arrange the three force vectors head-to-tail and state the feature of the finished diagram that shows equilibrium.
Which statement gives the definition of density?
A material has density 2.70 g cm^-3. What is this density in kg m^-3?
Samples P and Q have equal mass. The density of P is twice the density of Q. Which comparison of their volumes is correct?

options.A: The volume of P is half the volume of Q.
options.B: The volume of P equals the volume of Q.
options.C: The volume of P is twice the volume of Q.
options.D: The volume of P is four times the volume of Q.

questions.prompt: A solid cylindrical test piece has diameter 1.60 cm, length 0.750 m and mass 1.18 kg.

figure.purpose: Assess radius selection, geometric volume and density with consistent SI units.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a long solid cylinder. Mark the full circular width as diameter 1.60 cm, the axial length as 0.750 m and a separate mass label 1.18 kg. Include no radius value, volume formula, working or answer.
figure.alt_text: A solid cylinder has diameter 1.60 centimetres, length 0.750 metres and mass 1.18 kilograms.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of the test piece.

parts.label: (c)

questions.prompt: An aluminium mounting bracket has mass 0.540 kg and material density 2700 kg m^-3. Its outer dimensions fit exactly inside a rectangular box 12.0 cm by 5.00 cm by 5.00 cm, but the bracket has a large cut-out.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of aluminium in the bracket in m^3.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of the outer rectangular box in m^3.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why the value in (a) is the correct volume to use with the material density, rather than the value in (b).

questions.prompt: A solid metal sphere of radius 4.00 cm is held at rest by three coplanar forces. Its material density is 7800 kg m^-3. Its weight acts vertically downward. A horizontal cord pulls to the left. A second cord pulls up and to the right at 60.0 degrees above the horizontal. Use g = 9.81 N kg^-1.

figure.purpose: Assess a density calculation followed by a declared prior-learning equilibrium construction.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a small solid sphere treated as a point at its centre. Show one downward arrow labelled weight, one horizontal left cord force and one cord force directed 60.0 degrees above the horizontal to the right. Label radius 4.00 cm and density 7800 kg m^-3 nearby. Give no force magnitudes, components, triangle or answer.
figure.alt_text: A sphere is in equilibrium under its weight, a horizontal leftward cord force and an angled cord force sixty degrees above the horizontal.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of the sphere in m^3.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the weight of the sphere.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Sketch a closed head-to-tail force triangle for the three forces. Label the angle that allows the angled cord force to be related to the weight.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the force in the angled cord.
